ray-ds

Web components (Shadow DOM, no dependencies) inspired by shadcn/ui (semantic tokens, copy-the-code distribution) and Mantine (10-shade color scales, sizes xs–xl, color + variant on every component).

ray-ds is framework-agnostic. The components are standard custom elements: use them in any web app — plain HTML, React or Vue, in a browser or any webview. Nothing in a component requires raylang.

It comes with extras for raylang apps. It loads as plain ES modules from ray://app in a std/ui window with no build step, all its tooling (tokens, contrast checks, docs, webview tests) is written in raylang in tools/, and the examples are raylang apps. A native bridge (ray_ds/bridge in the program, core/raylang.js in the page) gives the components what a browser cannot: system file dialogs with real paths (ray-file-upload native, ray-path-input) and native confirmations (confirmDialog()). Planned: native menus in the command palette, window chrome, and a raylang package that serves the whole design system without npm. See RAYLANG.md.

Layout

tokens.toml            design tokens: the single source of truth
ray-ds.toml            npm package metadata (scope, version)
src/core/core.js       RayElement base class, css``, define(), theme API
src/core/styles.js     shared sizes, radius, color variants, loader
src/core/form.js       FormControl / FieldControl (ElementInternals, label/description/error)
src/core/floating.js   base of popover/menu/tooltip (Popover API, trigger wiring)
src/core/position.js   anchored placement with flip and shift
src/core/focus.js      tabbables through shadow roots and slots
src/core/host.js       the native host registry components ask (file dialogs, confirm)
src/core/raylang.js    the page's half of the raylang bridge: enableRaylang()
src/core/base.css      optional document defaults (layer ray.base)
src/core/core.d.ts     hand-written types of the core runtime
src/integrations/      React and Vue runtime helpers (createComponent)
src/components/<name>/ <name>.js + component.toml (metadata) + example.html
src/index.js           generated: imports every component
dist/                  generated: tokens.css, tokens.json
docs/                  generated: index.html, foundations.html, components.html (the catalog), components/<component>.html (a page each, and all.html with every one), code/<component>.html (each example's code, loaded on demand)
index.html             generated: redirects the server root to docs/
tests/                 *.test.js run in the real webview + harness.js
tools/                 raylang project: the ray-ds CLI
ray_ds/                raylang package: bridge.ray, the program's half of the bridge
packages/               generated npm packages: elements, react, vue
examples/desktop-form/ std/ui app using components copied with `add`
examples/react-app/    std/ui + Vite + React app using @ray-ds/react
examples/vue-app/      std/ui + Vite + Vue app using @ray-ds/vue
examples/extending/    app components on the extension API (+ `wrap` output)

Components

Category Tags
Buttons ray-button (incl. raised: a physical key that sinks when pressed), ray-icon-button, ray-toggle (two-state, aria-pressed; a raised one latches down), ray-toggle-group (single or multiple selection, joined or spaced), ray-button-group
Inputs ray-input, ray-number-input (+/− with hold-to-repeat, min/max/step, decimals, prefix/suffix, thousands), ray-combobox (a searchable select; multiple chips, creatable tags, clearable, groups), ray-search, ray-textarea, ray-select, ray-checkbox + ray-checkbox-group (one entry per value, max, required), ray-switch, ray-radio-group + ray-radio, ray-segmented-control, ray-slider, ray-date-picker + ray-calendar, ray-color-picker + ray-color-input (saturation area, hue and opacity sliders, swatches; a text field with the picker in a dropdown and an eyedropper; hex, rgb or hsl with or without alpha), ray-file-upload (drop zone: drag, click or paste; type/size/count checks; files listed as attachments; submitted with the form; native: real paths from the system dialog in a std/ui window), ray-path-input (a file, folder or save path; Browse… opens the system dialog in a std/ui window)
Navigation ray-tabs + ray-tab + ray-tab-panel, ray-nav-link, ray-sidebar + ray-sidebar-group (icon rail on wide screens, drawer on narrow ones), ray-bottom-nav + ray-bottom-nav-item (a phone app's tab bar: icons, labels, badges, a raised action, hides on scroll), ray-breadcrumbs + ray-breadcrumb (collapsible with max-items), ray-stepper + ray-step (wizards: loading, error, revisit completed steps), ray-pagination
Overlays ray-dialog (+ confirmDialog()), ray-drawer (any edge, modal or modeless), ray-popover, ray-tooltip, ray-menu + ray-menu-item / -label / -divider (also as context menu), ray-command-palette (⌘K)
Data display ray-timeline + ray-timeline-item (reached items, icon or avatar bullets, line variants), ray-icon, ray-badge, ray-avatar, ray-indicator (a dot or label on any element), ray-blockquote, ray-code (copy, line numbers, highlighted and diff lines; a built-in highlighter or any library via setHighlighter()), ray-kbd (raised, filled or outline), ray-accordion + ray-accordion-item, ray-table, ray-stat, ray-carousel (scroll-snap, swipe, autoplay), ray-attachment + ray-attachments
Feedback ray-alert, ray-spinner, ray-progress, ray-empty-state, ray-skeleton, ray-notification + ray-toaster (notify() with an optional action, updateNotification(), hideNotification(); a stack that spreads on hover, tap or focus, swipe to dismiss)
Layout ray-app-shell (header, navbar, main, aside, footer; a phone layout with a bottom bar below its breakpoint, measured on itself), ray-app-bar (a phone screen's top bar: back, title, actions; elevates or hides on scroll), ray-stack, ray-group, ray-grid (columns per width of the grid itself, spans, auto-fill), ray-container, ray-center, ray-scroll-area (themed scrollbar, edge shadows, ray-reach-end), ray-card, ray-separator, ray-split (resizable panes), ray-statusbar + ray-statusbar-item, ray-aspect-ratio

Server-rendered pages without JS get <table class="ray-table"> (plus ray-table-striped, ray-table-bordered) from base.css. | Theme | ray-theme-toggle |

Shared conventions (Mantine-style): size = xs…xl (default sm), radius, color = a palette color or any CSS color (default: primary), variant (filled, light, outline, subtle, default…). Form controls are form-associated: they submit under name, validate (required, pattern, type=email…), reset with the form and follow a disabled <fieldset>; they take label, description and error and wire the ARIA inside their shadow root. The value/checked attributes are initial values; the properties hold the current ones.

Overlays use the platform: ray-dialog is a native modal <dialog>; popovers, menus, tooltips and the toaster are [popover] elements in the top layer (never clipped, above everything), positioned in JS (core/position.js: flip + shift) since CSS anchor positioning is not in every webview yet. Keyboard behavior follows the WAI-ARIA patterns (menu button, tabs, accordion, radio group). While a modal dialog is open, notifications move into it so they stay clickable (a modal makes the rest of the page inert). Full API: docs/components.html (generated from each component.toml).

Variants

Component variant
button, icon-button filled · light · outline · subtle · default · transparent · gradient
badge light · filled · outline · dot · default · gradient
alert light · filled · outline · default · transparent
avatar light · filled · outline · default
card default · filled · outline
checkbox, radio (group or radio) filled · outline
input, textarea, select default · filled · unstyled
tabs default · outline · pills
accordion default · contained · separated · filled
nav-link light · filled · subtle
separator solid · dashed · dotted
statusbar default · accent

Color variants take any palette color or CSS color in color; gradient takes gradient="from to [deg]" (default: the --ray-gradient-* tokens; the text is white, so keep both ends dark enough). Your own variants: RayButton.extendStyles(css`[data-variant="brand"] { … }`) — see EXTENDING.md.

Icons

Every icon a component draws (close, chevrons, check, search, sort…) comes from one registry. Switch the whole set, or add names for <ray-icon>:

import { setIcons, iconNames } from "@ray-ds/elements";
setIcons({ close: '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">…</svg>', "chevron-down": svgElement, logo: "…" });

Icons are SVG markup (or an SVGElement) drawn with currentColor; mounted components repaint. --ray-icon-size and --ray-icon-stroke tune them system-wide. In your markup: <ray-icon name="info" label="Information"> (decorative without label). Register icons from your code only — the markup is inserted as HTML.

Commands

Run from ray-ds/ (or ray-ds/tools/):

ray run tools/src/main.ray build                 # tokens + docs + package
ray run tools/src/main.ray tokens [--check]      # tokens.toml -> dist/tokens.*, docs/foundations.html
ray run tools/src/main.ray docs                  # component.toml + *.md -> docs/ (site), src/index.js
ray run tools/src/main.ray add button input --into ../my-app/assets/ray-ds
ray run tools/src/main.ray package               # packages/{elements,react,vue}
ray run tools/src/main.ray site --base /ray-ds/  # build, then the site ready to publish in dist/site/
ray run tools/src/main.ray wrap --components DIR --out DIR   # types + wrappers for an app's components
ray run tools/src/main.ray webtest [FILTER]      # tests/*.test.js in a std/ui webview
(cd tools && ray test)                           # unit tests of the tools

Brand

The mark ("Kit") is three tiles of the raylang ocean palette plus the raylang emblem as one more piece. docs generates it from tools/src/site/brand.ray into brand/: logo.svg (light grounds), logo-dark.svg, logo-16.svg (without Manta's horns, per the raylang brand manual), icon.svg (app icon) and favicon.svg. The wordmark is "ray" in ray blue, the dot in aqua, "ds" in ink.

Viewing the docs

Serve the ray-ds directory itself (not docs/) and open the URL it prints:

cd ray-ds
ray serve . --port 0      # prints: serving . at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/

http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ redirects to the site in /docs/: the landing, this guide, the components, the foundations (token specimen), extending and charts — all generated by docs/tokens from component.toml, tokens.toml and the .md files, inside the layout of tools/src/site/layout.ray.html (a compiled raylang template; its CSS, JS and logo live in site/). The pages load ../dist and ../src, so served from docs/ (or opened as file://, where ES modules do not load) they show a banner saying so instead of rendering. --port 0 picks a free port; --port 8123 works too if you want a fixed one.

tokens fails if a [checks] aa pair is below 4.5:1 in either scheme, and warns for every palette color whose filled/light/outline variant text is.

Adding components to an app

add copies, shadcn-style: the code becomes the app's own.

<into>/tokens.css  base.css  core/*.js  components/<name>/…  index.js

It also copies what a component requires (switch brings checkbox), regenerates index.js with every component present, and never replaces a file the app has modified unless --overwrite (it reports it instead). --all adds everything. In a std/ui app, serve the directory with ui.mount_dir("", "assets") (or ui.mount_embed in a bundle) and load:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="ray-ds/tokens.css">
<script type="module" src="ray-ds/index.js"></script>

See examples/desktop-form (ray run src/main.ray --check fills and submits its form by script and checks what reaches the raylang side).

React and Vue

package generates three npm packages from the same component.toml files:

Package Contents
@ray-ds/elements the components, tokens.css, base.css, index.js (registers every element, re-exports the API), ray-ds.d.ts (a class per element, HTMLElementTagNameMap, typed detail of events), custom-elements.json, vscode.html-custom-data.json
@ray-ds/react a component per element (RayButton…): declared props are set as DOM properties, events are on + PascalCase (onRaySelect, onChange); React 18 and 19
@ray-ds/vue a component per element with v-model where it makes sense (value, checked, open), app.use(RayDs) and GlobalComponents types 
// React
import "@ray-ds/elements/tokens.css";
import { RayInput, RayMenu, RayMenuItem, RayButton } from "@ray-ds/react";

<RayInput label="Name" value={name} onInput={(e) => setName(e.currentTarget.value)} />
<RayMenu onRaySelect={(e) => run(e.detail.value)}>
  <RayButton slot="trigger">Actions</RayButton>
  <RayMenuItem value="rename">Rename</RayMenuItem>
</RayMenu>
<!-- Vue (app.use(RayDs) in main.ts) -->
<RayInput v-model="name" label="Name" required />
<RaySwitch v-model="enabled" label="Enabled" />
<RayDialog v-model="open" label="Confirm" @ray-close="onClose">…</RayDialog>

Use them from an app with file: dependencies on ray-ds/packages/* and resolve.preserveSymlinks: true (Vite) / "preserveSymlinks": true (tsconfig), so react/vue resolve from the app and a re-run of package is picked up without reinstalling. The examples are raylang apps made with ray new <name> --frontend react-ts|vue-ts:

cd examples/react-app              # or examples/vue-app
npm --prefix frontend install
ray dev                            # Vite dev server (HMR) inside a std/ui window
npm --prefix frontend run typecheck  # the generated .d.ts checked by tsc / vue-tsc
npm --prefix frontend run build && ray run src/main.ray --check

--check drives the built page in the real webview like a user (typing, choosing, submitting, the menu opening a controlled dialog) and checks both directions: what reaches raylang through window.ray.request, and the framework state rendered back into the components. The dev servers use high ports (45173, 45174).

Using it in a page

<link rel="stylesheet" href="ray-ds/dist/tokens.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="ray-ds/src/core/base.css"> <!-- optional -->
<script type="module" src="ray-ds/src/index.js"></script>

<ray-input label="Email" name="email" type="email" required></ray-input>
<ray-button type="submit">Save</ray-button>

Style your own markup with the tokens:

.panel {
  background: var(--ray-card);
  color: var(--ray-card-foreground);
  border: 1px solid var(--ray-border);
  border-radius: var(--ray-radius-default);
  padding: var(--ray-space-md);
  box-shadow: var(--ray-shadow-sm);
}

Tokens

Kind Example Notes
Palette --ray-blue-0 … --ray-blue-9 12 colors (open-color); scheme independent
Variants --ray-blue-filled, -filled-hover, -light, -light-hover, -light-color, -outline, -outline-hover, -contrast per color, light/dark aware
Primary --ray-primary-6, --ray-primary-filled, … aliases of the primary color
Semantic --ray-background, --ray-foreground, --ray-primary, --ray-muted, --ray-border, --ray-ring, … what components and apps use
Scales --ray-space-*, --ray-radius-*, --ray-font-size-*, --ray-control-height-*, --ray-shadow-*, --ray-duration-*, --ray-z-*

Breakpoints are exported to dist/tokens.json only (custom properties cannot be used in @media).

Charts

--ray-chart-1…8 (series, in order), --ray-chart-grid/-axis/-text/-tooltip… and chartTheme() for canvas libraries: recipes for Chart.js, uPlot and ECharts in CHARTS.md.

Theme and primary color

  • The theme follows the system by default (color-scheme: light dark and light-dark() values). Force it on the page or on any subtree with data-theme="light" / data-theme="dark".

  • Switch the primary color of the page or a subtree with data-primary="violet" (any palette color).

  • From JS: setTheme("light" | "dark" | "system"), setPrimary("violet"), getTheme(), resolvedTheme(), onThemeChange(cb) from src/core/core.js. The page-level choice is persisted in localStorage when available and restored when core.js loads.

  • No flash on load: core.js is a module, so it restores the stored theme after the first paint — a page whose stored choice differs from the system flashes the other scheme. Apply it first with an inline script in <head>, before the stylesheets, and hide components until they are defined:

    <script>
  try {
    const t = localStorage.getItem("ray-ds:theme");
    if (t === "light" || t === "dark") document.documentElement.dataset.theme = t;
    const p = localStorage.getItem("ray-ds:primary");
    if (p && p !== "custom") document.documentElement.dataset.primary = p;
  } catch {}
</script>
<style>:not(:defined) { visibility: hidden; }</style>

  • Any brand color: definePrimary("#7c3aed") (page) or definePrimary(color, { el }) (subtree) builds ten shades in OKLCH, picks white or black text by contrast (a bright color fills with itself and black text, like yellow), switches to data-primary="custom" and returns { shades, filled, contrast, ratio, aa }, warning below WCAG AA. Every variant follows the same rules as the palette colors.

  • Component defaults: configure({ defaults: { "ray-button": { variant: "light", size: "md" } } }) for whatever the markup and code leave unset.

Browser support: light-dark() and color-mix() — Safari/WebKit 17.5+, Chrome 123+, Firefox 120+ (WebKitGTK 2.44+, current Android WebView).

Overlay

Modal dialogs, drawers and the command palette darken the page with --ray-overlay and blur it with --ray-overlay-blur ([overlay] blur in tokens.toml, 4px by default; 0px turns it off). Change it for the whole app, a subtree or one element:

:root { --ray-overlay-blur: 8px; --ray-overlay: rgb(0 0 0 / 25%); }
.settings { --ray-overlay-blur: 0px; }
<ray-dialog overlay-blur="none" label="Plain backdrop">…</ray-dialog>

or as a default for every instance: configure({ defaults: { "ray-dialog": { overlayBlur: "12" } } }). The blur is dropped for users who ask for reduced transparency.

Extending

Components are classes on public bases (RayElement, FormControl, FieldControl, Floating) and an app can build on them or on any component: see EXTENDING.md — the contract, the three levels, extendStyles, configure({ defaults }) and wrap (types and React/Vue wrappers for an app's own components).

Writing a component

import { RayElement, css, define } from "../../core/core.js";

export class RayThing extends RayElement {
  static properties = { size: { type: String, reflect: true, default: "sm" } };
  static styles = [css`:host { display: inline-flex; }`];
  static template = `<span part="label"><slot></slot></span>`;
  update(changed) { /* sync the shadow DOM with the properties */ }
}
define("ray-thing", RayThing);
  • Styling hooks: tokens (CSS custom properties pierce the shadow root), ::part() and slots. Document them in component.toml.
  • Events: a value change is a plain change (and input), read from the element; anything else is this.emit("ray-something", detail) (bubbles, composed). See "Events" in EXTENDING.md.
  • Properties set before the element is defined (React/Vue) are picked up on connection.
  • Focus rings: give the focusable element class="focus-ring".
  • Shared styles: sizeStyles, radiusStyles, variantStyles + applyColor(el, color) from core/styles.js; form controls extend FieldControl from core/form.js.
  • Add component.toml (API) and example.html, run build, and cover the behavior in tests/*.test.js.

Roadmap

  1. Foundations — tokens, theme, core runtime, generator, webview tests ✅
  2. Primitives — buttons, inputs, display, card, separator; add; component docs ✅
  3. Overlays and interaction — dialog, popover, tooltip, menu, notifications, tabs, segmented control, accordion ✅
  4. Integrations — generated React and Vue wrappers, .d.ts, custom-elements.json, example apps ✅
  5. App composites — table, command palette, split panes, nav links, status bar, progress, slider, stat, empty state ✅
  6. Adoption — pilot in ray-remote, then rayauth

Charts: ray-ds draws none (decision: option A). It provides the chart palette (--ray-chart-1…8 + chrome tokens, checked at build time for contrast, separation and color blindness) and chartTheme() / onChartThemeChange() for chart libraries — see CHARTS.md. Own chart components (SVG primitives; an adapter for dense real-time series) stay open for later, when an app needs them.
